Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: E-SIRCEV (Electronic System of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics) was launched March 2019 and is operational in 121 of 164 registries. It registers births, deaths, marriages and assigns NUIC at birth. The system links health units for birth/death notifications (NUIC assigned at birth even without a name). The X-Road interoperability pilot uses DNRN (which manages e-SIRCEV) as the data source for birth certificate verification. World Bank Datasphere article notes 59,000+ birth certificates and 42,000+ IDs issued during integrated civil registration and ID mobile brigade campaigns. Score 4: partially integrated with the interoperability platform (X-Road pilot).

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: Mozambique has NUIC (Unique Citizen Identification Number, Decreto 44/2010). E-SIRCEV civil registration system assigns NUIC at birth and uses it as a unique identifier. DNIC (National Directorate of Civil Identification) issues ID cards linked to NUIC. X-Road interoperability pilot uses birth certificate verification from DNRN to issue IDs (DNIC) as the first use case. Nationwide free ID campaign launched Nov 2023 (140,000+ IDs issued). However, separate systems exist per sector with limited coordination. Score 3: under development.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Mozambique has Decree 67/2017 (Interoperability Regulation) - establishes framework for data sharing and interoperability among public entities, and between public and private entities. Electronic Transactions Law (Law No. 3/2017) includes e-government provisions. INTIC is updating the interoperability framework (under revision, World Bank EDGE support). No comprehensive data protection law in force (draft underway, MCTD-led). No independent data protection authority exists yet. Score 2: partial - interoperability decree exists but no comprehensive cross-government data sharing law.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Mozambique's National Digital Transformation Strategy drafting process launched February 2026. A Public Sector Digital Transformation Strategy is being developed under EDGE project. Information Society Policy (2018) exists but with 'limited implementation'. The 2025-2044 National Development Strategy includes digital transformation as a pillar. National Data Governance Policy (zero draft 2 circulated Nov 2025) is under development. No comprehensive approved data exchange strategy. Data exchange is mentioned within broader DPI/digital transformation agenda. Score 2: mentioned in broader strategy but no standalone comprehensive framework.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: INAGE (National Institute of Electronic Government) is implementing a government interoperability platform using Estonia's X-Road technology. The initial use case is birth certificate verification for ID issuance (DNIC) and tax IDs (NUIT), with a working group of INAGE, DNIC, DNRN, and AT. However, the World Bank/AfDB April 2025 diagnostic reports that data systems are fragmented, with 'weak interconnectivity' and reliance on email/flash drives. The platform is under development. E-SIRCEV (civil registration) was officially launched in 2019 and deployed in 121 of 164 registries. GovNet (government electronic network) managed by INAGE is operational. Status: under development with limited initial operational deployments. Score 3: under development.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: About 80% of Mozambicans were offline in 2024 (ITU). More than half the population lacks official ID. 65% of population lives in rural areas with limited infrastructure. The CIS/Digital ID study notes only 35% of population has smartphones. E-SIRCEV is digital but many registry operations remain on paper. Score 1: limited accessibility.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Mozambique ratified the AU Malabo Convention (Resolution No. 5/2019). Electronic Transactions Law (No. 2/2017) restricts cross-border data transfers to foreign institutions unless mandated by law or court order. Decree 67/2017 on e-government interoperability includes data security and confidentiality provisions. National Data Governance Policy (zero draft 2025) includes sovereignty provisions. However, no data protection law is in force (draft underway) and no independent data protection authority exists. Score 2: limited controls.

Definition: Extent to which provincial/state and local governments participate in the data exchange
Comments: E-SIRCEV is deployed in provincial directorates and civil registry offices (121 of 164 registries). GovNet provides network to government institutions. However, 65% of population lives in rural areas with limited internet (80% offline per ITU 2024). Free ID campaign had mobile brigades reaching rural areas but digital systems fragmented. Sub-national government participation in data exchange is being planned through the Digital Transformation Strategy. Score 2: planned expansion to sub-national level.
